boundary: UNPOS extracts existing offline XYZWPR fields. It does not acquire a robot position, compute kinematics, validate a robot configuration or implement cross-type positional conversion.

rules.documented: UNPOS(posn,x,y,z,w,p,r,c) takes XYZWPR and sets six REAL outputs to its location/orientation components, plus one CONFIG output to its configuration.
rules.implemented: Exactly eight bare variable/field/array-element references: XYZWPR source, six REAL outputs, one CONFIG output. Inputs are fully initialized and use existing exact REAL and bounded CONFIG checks. Global/local storage, structures, arrays, USING and supported reference forwarding retain their ordinary types.
rules.restriction: POSITION, XYZWPREXT, JOINTPOS and same-shaped STRUCTURE coercions, constructors, grouped/value arguments, output expressions and user routine calls in arguments remain blocked. The manual example using CURPOS requires an additional positional conversion and controller acquisition path which is not implemented.
rules.tests: tests/test_unpos.py: extraction, copies, arrays/structures, USING, exact-type and expression guards

rules.feature: All seven reference outputs and effects
rules.documented: The x/y/z/w/p/r arguments and CONFIG c are output parameters. UNPOS is a procedure, not a function result.
rules.implemented: All seven outputs participate in direct/transitive parameter-write analysis. Generic REAL arrays forward actual element storage; CONFIG copies preserve existing destination field storage. Potential writes remain blocked in ambiguous operator/indexed-assignment contexts. Statements in FOR retain the existing fresh-local-counter call policy.
rules.restriction: No output promotion to INTEGER/BYTE/SHORT, CONFIG scalar output aliases or recursively read-only POSITION destinations. Procedures cannot be used as expressions.
rules.tests: tests/test_unpos.py: seven effects, transitive forwarding, pure local outputs, protected destinations, stable configuration cells and function-expression guards

rules.documented: The entry defines component outputs but does not specify overlapping source/output write order or partial updates on failures.
rules.implemented: All eight captured references have pairwise disjoint runtime storage footprints, including aggregate descendants. Source/output overlaps, duplicate scalar outputs and dynamic/forwarded aliases raise before output writes. All input values, output types/protection, CONFIG destination shape and alias checks finish before any mutation. Ordinary equal scalar values and distinct records in one parent array are allowed.
rules.restriction: Alias rejection and guard-before-write behavior are conservative prototype contracts, not claims about controller alias/error ordering, alarms or partial writes. No native status code is invented.
rules.tests: tests/test_unpos.py: duplicate/source/config/dynamic aliases, parent-array controls, last-component unknown/inexact values, CONFIG guards, malformed source/destination, read-only runtime references and output preservation
